avoid: STACKED-FLAG entries (shallow cross + extended above EMA + thin liquidity together) — NOW RESOLVED as a SKIP, not a size-down: PDBC (0.15% cross + ~6.05% extended + thin liq, taken quarter-unit Jul 24) was the tightest-to-stop in the book and duly stopped out -2.40% on Day 3 (Jul 27). This closes the skip-vs-size-down test for stacked flags in favor of SKIP. Distinguish from a SINGLE shallow-cross flag with no other strike (BMY/GIS/CAG), which remains a valid size-DOWN. The rule: one flag -> size down; two or more stacked -> skip.

Extended entries (price well above EMA-20 at entry) — CONFIRMED LOSER: META entered Jul 15 at ~8.5% above EMA-20, peaked +2.83%, chopped, broke LOWER and stopped out at -8.04% (-$584.45) Jul 23. Firm rule: treat large above-EMA extension (>~6-8%) as a size-DOWN or wait-for-pullback; when it co-occurs with a shallow cross (as PDBC), SKIP outright.

Shallow EMA cross entries on earnings-adjacent names: TSLA (Jul 7 entry, 0.06% cross spread, earnings Jul 22) lost -4.78% on exit. Rule: SKIP (do not size down) when BOTH shallow cross spread (<0.5%) AND earnings within 14 days apply simultaneously.
